title: Nonreciprocal Magnon Hanle Effect in Antiferromagnetic $α$-Fe$_2$O$_3$
authors: Janine Gückelhorn, Sebastián de-la-Peña, Monika Scheufele, Matthias Grammer, Matthias Opel, Stephan Geprägs, Juan Carlos Cuevas, Rudolf Gross, Hans Huebl, Akashdeep Kamra, Matthias Althammer
abstract: The precession of the magnon pseudospin about the equilibrium pseudofield, the latter capturing the nature of magnonic eigenexcitations in an antiferromagnet, gives rise to the magnon Hanle effect. Its realization via electrically injected and detected spin transport in an antiferromagnetic insulator demonstrates its high potential for devices and as a convenient probe for magnon eigenmodes and the underlying spin interactions in the antiferromagnet. Here, we observe a non-reciprocity in the Hanle signal measured in alpha-Fe2O3 using two spatially separated Pt electrodes as spin injector and detector. Interchanging their roles alters the detected magnon spin signal. The recorded difference depends on the applied magnetic field and reverses sign when the signal passes its nominal maximum at the so-called compensation field. Our findings unlock the high potential of antiferromagnetic magnonics towards the realization of electronics-inspired phenomena.
summary: This experimental work investigates the magnon Hanle effect in antiferromagnetic alpha-Fe2O3 using electrical spin injection and detection. The key finding is the observation of a nonreciprocal magnon spin signal, which changes when the roles of the injector and detector are swapped. This demonstrates the potential of antiferromagnetic magnonics for advanced spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to observe and characterize the nonreciprocal magnon Hanle effect in an antiferromagnetic insulator.
main_result: The researchers successfully demonstrated a nonreciprocal magnon spin signal in alpha-Fe2O3, where reversing the roles of the spin injector and detector alters the measured signal.
method: The experiment utilizes a non-local, two-terminal geometry to measure magnon spin currents via electrical injection and detection using Pt electrodes.
model_or_system: The physical system is alpha-Fe2O3 thin films coupled with Pt electrodes. The phenomenon studied is the magnon Hanle effect, which involves the precession of the magnon pseudospin.
key_observables: The magnon spin signal ($R_{	ext{magn}} = V_{	ext{det}}/I_{	ext{inj}}$), its dependence on the external magnetic field, and the difference in signal when the injector/detector roles are interchanged.
important_parameters: The external magnetic field ($\mathbf{H}$), particularly the compensation field (6 T) and the in-plane rotation angle ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The nonreciprocity is attributed to the presence of an antisymmetric magnonic pseudofield, which is a key theoretical deduction.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) sketches the sample setup and angle dependence. Figure 1(b) shows the field dependence confirming the compensation field. Figure 1(c) compares forward and backward propagation signals, highlighting the nonreciprocity.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, measurements of the Hanle effect, and then focuses on demonstrating and analyzing the nonreciprocal nature of the signal as a function of magnetic field and angle.
why_interesting: The observation of nonreciprocity in magnonics, linked to an antisymmetric pseudofield, provides a platform for realizing electronics-inspired phenomena in magnetic materials, relevant for understanding spin-orbit coupling effects in quantum systems.
